lawyer:
AF Hasan Ariff with Ramzan Ali Sikder and Abdullah M Hasan Advocates-For the Petitioner.
SM Muniruzzaman, AAG-For the Respondents.
parties:
Unique Hotel and Resorts Limited ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
National Board of Revenue and others   ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the arbitrary and discriminatory refusal of exemption from payment of customs duties, VAT and other taxes pursuant to section 20 of the Customs Act, 1969 and section 14 of the VAT Act, 1991 against the importation of various capital machinery for setting up a five star hotel as contained in Nothi No. 2( 15) Shu: Mu (moukuf)/2000 dated 1-3-20005 (Annexure-A) and non-consideration of the petitioner's application dated 9-8-2006 (Annexure-P) and the assessment of duties and taxes at a higher rate as evident from the Bill of Entry No.C-16047 dated 20-8-2006 (Annexure-A-1) in disregard of the concessionary rate at 5% as contained in SRO No .114 dated 8-6-2006 should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and unconstitutional and void being violative of the fundamental rights of the petitioner guaranteed under Articles 27, 31, 40 and 42 of the Constitution and why the respondents should not be directed to grant exemptions to the petitioner in respect of the petitioner's imported capital machineries as per SRO No.114/2006 dated 8-6-2006 read with section 20 of the Customs Act, 1969 and section 14 of the VAT Act, 1991 or such other or further orders as to this court may seem fit and proper." 

 4. Another applicant M/s Sarina Inn Limited, Dhaka (the Sarina, in brief) applied for similar exemption for setting up its hotel project. The respondents granted exemption to the Sarina in respect of much wider categories of articles by an order dated 6-5-2002. The petitioner has as many as seven applications during 20-7-2002 to 15-12- 2005 but without any success. Finally, the petitioner submitted an application before the Minister, Ministry of Finance and Planning on 6-1-2005 seeking exemption under section 20 of the Customs Act and section 14 of the VAT Act, but without result. The petitioner imported electrical refrigerators under Letter of Credit No. 0746-0601-0122 dated 4-6-2006 issued by the City Bank Limited, Kawran Bazar Branch, Dhaka. The respondents have granted exemption in terms of SRO 158 and section 20 of the Act and section 14 of the VAT Act in favour of the Sarina by an order dated 6-5-2002, Sea Gull Hotels Limited by an order dated 3-5-2001, M/s Nandan Park Limited by order dated 14-12-2002, M/s. Bashundhara City, Abul Khair Steel Products and Shah Cement Industries Limited. But till date the petitioner did not get any response. The impugned order of refusal, assessment of customs duties and taxes treating the goods as commercial imports instead of concessionary rate on the capital machineries imported, non-consideration of the petitioner's application and failure to release of the petitioner's goods at concessionary rate of 5% in terms of SRO No. 114/Ain/2006/2106/Shalko dated 8-6-2006 (SRO 114) are without lawful authority. 

 6. Respondent No.1 i.e. NBR contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition contending inter alia, that the Government under section 20 of the Customs Act may allow full or partial exemption from statutory duties on goods under certain circumstances. Such exemption does not create any vested right in favour of the importers. Assessment of customs duties at the enhanced rate was not illegal on 1-12-2001. Respondent Nos. 3 and 4 by an order dated 9-5-2002 granted exemption of duties and taxes on certain machineries of the petitioner. Subsequently, that exemption order was .revised on 19-10-2004 and some other machineries were included in it. Respondent No.2 refused to give exemption from payment of duties and taxes in favour of the Sena Hotel Developments Limited by an order dated 14-12-2004 and others. Since the petitioner has been enjoying partial benefit from exemption of payment of duties and taxes on certain articles/machineries it cannot claim for further benefit on the basis of the same recommendation which has already been acted upon. The Government has a power to grant exemption which can be partial or whole subject to certain conditions. No importers can claim absolute exemption as of right. The petitioner filed an application for concessional rate of duties on imported machineries and others which do not fall under SRO No. 158 and or SRO 114. Since the petitioner's items are not included in these SROs and it is not legally entitled to get the benefit of SRO No.158 or SRO No.114 as of right. This writ petition is misconceived, not maintainable and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 14. It transpires from the materials on record (Annexure-P to the Writ Petition) that the Managing Director of the petitioner applied to NBR for release of the imported machineries under bill of entry No. C/1607 dated 20-8-2006 without payment of duties and taxes for construction of hotel. The petitioner failed to produce any letter showing that it was refused by NBR but photostat copy of the note sheet of NBR has been annexed to the writ petition. The photostat copy is not legible. However, it appears from the typed copy that exemption from the duties and taxes for 5 items were allowed to the petitioner and it was admittedly extended for certain other items. The petitioner applied for importation of other materials with the same facilities and the Chairman wrote in the note "may regret" and NBR decided to inform it to the petitioner. However, it is not disputed that NBR refused to) exempt the duties and taxes at concession rate of 5% in terms of SRO No. 114 and pursuant 10 section 20 of the Customs Act and also section 14 of the VAT Act. 

 17. In note No.73 dated 3-12-2003 (annexure-3 to the affidavit-in-opposition) it was stated that the Minister earlier approved exemption permission to the petitioner and the Sarina on 24-4-2004 and 25-3-2003. However, the Minister subsequently refused to approve similar proposal on 12-9-2002 and 25-3-2003.This writ petition is not over challenging the said order. In the instant case, the petitioner filed another application for exemption of other machineries with the same benefit as has been granted to it earlier relating to some other capital machineries and from Annexure-A to the writ petition it transpires that Board refused the same on 16-2-2005 by note No. 154. Therefore, it cannot be presumed that due to a direction passed in the year 2003, the Board refused to consider the application of the petitioner in the year 2006 at the direction of the Minister. Moreover, there is no indication in the note that the refusal was made at the direction of the Minister. Furthermore, admittedly NBR by letter dated 19-10-2004 extended its exemption to the petitioner on some additional items which is after the order of the Minister. Therefore, there is no iota of evidence showing that the impugned refusal was made by NBR at the direction of the Minister.
